contract: Run one OS command per request with bounded slots and queue, an absolute deadline, group-scoped termination performed by erlexec's port program, and an observed result mapped to the shared delivery result; the Adapter never signals itself.
limits: Not security isolation: no sandbox, container, seccomp, path confinement or network isolation; no shell parsing; stdin is /dev/null.

Terminations the provider performs on request (cancel, caller or owner death) report no ending signal and are unknown; a member that ignores SIGTERM after the leader exits, a descendant that leaves the group, and the provider port program's own death are declared residuals.

An exec failure after pre-dispatch validation is reported by the provider as exit 1 and appears as completed; a SIGTERM or SIGKILL status reported at or after the deadline instant is attributed to the provider's watchdog and cannot be told from a self-signalled command; group observation with pgrep reports what the process table shows, not a proof of cleanup; one OS at a time.

grounding.claim: Named real-process scenarios (transition rows T1-T23, T26-T29, controls C1-C3, review findings F1-F7, provider protocol P1, consumer priv dir) with group emptiness observed by the test's own pgrep; finite observations on one OS per run, not proofs.
Provider application stop (T24) and port-program SIGKILL (T25): the orphan is reported, not hidden; finite observations.
Every Adapter result row validates through Elzoo.Envelope.validate_result/1 with correlation fallback and the unchanged sidecar; wait-status decoding.
Delivery-result maps are checked by the named checker Elzoo.Envelope.validate_result/1 at construction; Elixir typespecs are documentation.

Relies on erlexec 2.6.0: group creation ({group, 0}, kill_group), wall-clock timeout with SIGTERM then SIGKILL after kill_timeout, linked-owner stop, finalize on port EOF, exit-status report, env clear; its masked status on stop and single at-exit TERM are pinned implementation observations, not promises.
Relies on pinned GenServer, Supervisor, DynamicSupervisor, Process.monitor and Process.send_after semantics.
Relies on ETS ownership, link and monitor signal ordering (messages before the exit signal) and the 4_294_967_295 ms timer bound.

The OS delivers a group signal to every member; PID 1 reaps orphans; the provider's check-to-signal gap does not coincide with a PID wrap; a C++ toolchain builds the port program; pgrep and the POSIX sh used by the fixture behave as observed on macOS and Ubuntu.

telemetry.contract: No event, log or measurement is emitted; a future event family must exclude the command line, arguments, environment and output (tested: no observation channel carries them today).

config.contract: Construction-time max_concurrent, queue_limit, queue_timeout_ms, grace_s, observe_timeout_ms, max_output_bytes, pgrep_path, now_unix_ms; per-call deadline_unix_ms or max_run_ms, cwd and environment allowlist; validated with the OTP timer bound; no hot update, a change needs a new instance.

control.contract: cancel/2 by run ref: acceptance ({:ok, :requested}); a repeated cancel answers {:ok, :already_requested} for a running run and for one of the last 1024 queued runs settled by cancellation (it acknowledges the duplicate request); every other finished or foreign ref gets {:error, :unknown_run}; a queued run becomes rejected{cancelled}, a running run is stopped through the provider and reported unknown{provider_masked_stop}; no pause or drain; stopping the instance terminates running commands through the provider.
